messages:
karen: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands  consolidating a few leadership Qs so we can publish a short FAQ. Keeping answers bite-size.

karen: 1) What's a one-line explanation of why Redwood exists that non-technical execs will remember?

otto: "We make inference predictable and economical so engineering teams can ship LLM features without surprise ops costs." Short, customer-oriented.

karen: 2) How do we succinctly differentiate vs cloud provider endpoints in a sales conversation?

mia: Say: cloud endpoints are about model access; Redwood is about predictable production serving: latency, cost controls, and rollout safety. Follow with a quick example (we reduced token costs by 30% for a C2B chat workload via batching + cache).

pranav: Add: mention our model-variant fallback routing that keeps apps online during capacity issues. That's a tangible reliability win.

karen: 3) Messaging tone: should top-of-funnel use "build vs buy" or product-differentiation language?

otto: Lead with "build vs buy" for engineering buyers because it addresses the core decision. For marketing assets frame it as "production-ready inference" to avoid upfront vendor bashing.

karen: 4) From a product roadmap POV, what's the single feature this quarter that signals we're executing on the strategy?

mia: The public persona->deployment playbook + the customer-run benchmark harness. If sales can hand a prospect a benchmark from our harness and an ops playbook, that's a big win.

pranav: Also shipping token-level cost breakdowns in the Console (visible to customers) is a critical product signal.

karen: 5) What public metrics can marketing show that matter but don't leak internal SLAs?

otto: Publish a reference p95 latency for a standard prompt size, model catalog count, and a sample per-token cost range for a common configuration. Keep SLO attainment internal.

karen: 6) Competitor language: should we create a "compare" FAQ with explicit vendor rows?

mia: Yes, but keep it gated: public FAQ high level, downloadable appendix with explicit comparisons (TCO, latency) for sales/technical audiences. Avoid naming in hero content.

ops-bot: All-hands slides + recording -> https://redwood.internal/all-hands/3344556677 (slides: strategy appendix attached)

karen: Thanks all. Action items: @mia draft the public 600-word FAQ, @otto prepare the compare appendix, @pranav pull one anonymized benchmark blurb. Planning to publish next week if legal signs off. Closing thread after follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
